made: Made to line up with UFLI Foundations' scope and sequence, by lesson number. UFLI didn't make it and hasn't endorsed it. The descriptions are ours.
source: Lesson numbers from UFLI Foundations' scope and sequence (2022) and the concept on each of its decodable passages, checked 18 October 2026. The route was not derived from them.

1.note: Open I beside closed it, on the first day. UFLI comes to open and closed syllables at lessons 66 and 68.

3.note: An open vowel says its name from step 3, and y arrives as a vowel. UFLI teaches y as a consonant at lesson 30, and as the vowel of my at 73.

4.note: The rest of the single consonants are in place by this step. UFLI spends lessons 1 to 41 on single letters and short vowels.

6.note: Ll and ss arrive with kernel words (will, spell), with ck and tch beside them. UFLI practises clusters in its review lessons, 35 to 41.

7.note: No UFLI lesson teaches oul. The route reads would, could and should from a single analog.

8.note: The nearest UFLI lesson is 62, where silent-e words that break the pattern come up.

9.note: The vault arrives at step 9. UFLI begins silent e at lesson 54.

11.note: Ay, ee and igh arrive at step 11. UFLI begins vowel teams at lesson 84.

13.note: UFLI comes first with the -s ending, at lessons 20 and 21.

14.note: The box marks a pair stopping a reach, at the seam or inside a word. UFLI teaches the doubled spellings at 42, 44 and 69 to 71, and doubling at the seam at 107 and 108.

19.note: UFLI treats these as words learned by heart. The route reads them as a vowel borrowing another vowel's sound.

28.note: UFLI teaches th and wh as digraphs. The route comes back to them as a family of words.

contrasts.what: A vowel says its name in an open syllable

contrasts.ufli: lessons 73 and 74, after y as /y/ at 30
